constraints: Remain useful without an account or network connection
Version persisted state against the lesson content version
Provide explicit export and deletion controls
Do not store credentials, source secrets, or provider responses

candidates.name: Web Storage
candidates.summary: Persist a small JSON snapshot in localStorage with no added dependency; synchronous I/O and string-only values constrain growth.

evidence.locator: Concepts and usage: synchronous localStorage/sessionStorage operations and storage limits

candidates.name: Native IndexedDB
candidates.summary: Use the browser's asynchronous transactional structured-data store directly, accepting a larger application-owned adapter.

evidence.locator: IndexedDB description: significant structured data, indexes, transactions, and asynchronous operations

candidates.name: idb
candidates.summary: Use the small promise-based idb wrapper while retaining IndexedDB's stores, transactions, and versioned upgrade path.

evidence.locator: README: promise-based IndexedDB API, browser support, upgrade callback, and transaction completion

recommendation.rationale: It preserves a transactional, versioned local-first data model while reducing adapter complexity. Dependency adoption remains blocked until the spike measures bundle cost, migration behavior, and recovery from invalid state.

spike.question: Can idb persist versioned progress, mastery, resume position, and learner notes without corrupting state across real lesson revisions?
steps: Use an existing generated lesson artifact and its real content version; do not create demo learner data
Implement the same typed persistence adapter against native IndexedDB and idb on isolated branches
Exercise reload, upgrade, downgrade rejection, concurrent-tab writes, export, deletion, and invalid-record recovery
Record compressed bundle delta, migration duration, error behavior, and browser results
passCriteria: Content-version changes do not silently preserve invalid mastery
Learners can export and delete their local state
All measurements are captured from the current application and real generated lesson artifacts

constraints: Index only source-grounded fields emitted by the compiler
Keep navigation deterministic and usable without a hosted search service
Support keyboard operation and meaningful empty-result states
Do not expose private research artifacts in the browser index

candidates.name: Compiler-emitted concept index
candidates.summary: Emit a compact lesson, concept, prerequisite, and source index from the existing validated content graph and search it in-browser.

evidence.locator: runLessonPipeline checkpoints validated claims, plan, interactions, lesson, and evaluation artifacts

candidates.name: Pagefind
candidates.summary: Build a static search bundle after rendering, or use the Node API for non-static content, gaining a mature index at the cost of a post-build integration.

evidence.locator: Overview: indexes generated static HTML and emits a static search bundle
Node API: programmatic indexing including non-static or non-HTML content

recommendation.rationale: The content graph contains concepts and prerequisites that rendered-page search cannot infer reliably. Start with the compiler-owned semantic index, then rerun Pagefind at a larger corpus size if hand-owned ranking or payload size becomes the limiting factor.

spike.question: Can a compiler-emitted index make every currently generated lesson, concept, prerequisite, and cited source reachable with deterministic keyboard navigation?
steps: Build the index only from existing validated lesson and research artifacts
Add persistent course position, prerequisite breadcrumbs, next and previous actions, and search result explanations
Measure index size, query latency, zero-result behavior, keyboard flow, and source-field leakage
Run the same real corpus through Pagefind's Node API and record the comparative measurements
passCriteria: A learner can locate the current concept and prerequisite path
Search reaches lessons, concepts, and sources
Every lesson exposes a deterministic next action
The browser index contains no provider prompts, private notes, or unapproved research artifacts

constraints: Every visual must declare the relationship it teaches
Every visual needs a complete text equivalent and static fallback
Generated content may select only allowlisted declarative primitives
Quantitative scales and topology diagrams require different semantics

candidates.name: Custom semantic SVG primitives
candidates.summary: Extend the existing allowlisted schema and React renderer with purpose-built timelines, causal graphs, state machines, parameter plots, and annotated code.

evidence.locator: Allowlisted declarative lesson block and interaction contracts

candidates.name: Vega-Lite
candidates.summary: Use a declarative JSON grammar that compiles to Vega for interactive quantitative and multi-view plots.

evidence.locator: Overview: high-level JSON grammar for interactive multi-view visualizations that compiles to Vega
Vega-Lite paper: declarative grammar and compilation model

candidates.name: Hybrid semantic visual grammar
candidates.summary: Keep topology and mechanism diagrams in application-owned accessible primitives while restricting Vega-Lite to quantitative plots.

evidence.locator: Existing application-owned declarative visual renderer and text fallback behavior

recommendation.rationale: One generic diagram library would blur the distinction between quantitative encodings and mechanism topology. The hybrid keeps the generated contract semantic while avoiding custom scale and plotting machinery where Vega-Lite is strongest.

spike.question: Can one real mechanism be expressed as an accessible custom state or causal diagram and one real parameter relationship as Vega-Lite without arbitrary generated code?
steps: Select two relationships already supported by claims in the current research package
Render the topology relationship with a new allowlisted semantic primitive and the quantitative relationship with a restricted Vega-Lite spec
Verify schema rejection, static fallback, text equivalence, keyboard behavior, narrow layout, and reduced motion
Measure compressed bundle delta and renderer execution time before recommending a dependency
passCriteria: Every visual states the relationship it explains
Primitive contracts pass narrow-screen and keyboard tests
Generated lesson JSON cannot inject code, event handlers, remote data, or an unapproved Vega transform
